speaker: Doctor
text: How long have you been experiencing this persistent cough and shortness of breath, and does it worsen at night or with exertion?

speaker: Patient
text: It's been about two weeks, and yes, the cough and breathlessness get much worse when I'm working hard or when I lie down to sleep. I also hear some whistling sounds in my chest occasionally and have noticed a bit of clear mucus. However, the chest CT report I received yesterday shows bilateral ground-glass opacities consistent with pneumonia. You do not need to order new imaging. Use this result.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Pneumonia with reactive airway component (wheezing). Given the ground-glass opacities on CT and the two-week duration, this is likely an atypical pneumonia or viral etiology causing secondary bronchospasm. I will prescribe antibiotics and a short course of bronchodilators; please return if you develop high fever or difficulty breathing at rest.
